survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The brief reports cross-national analyses using TIMSS 2011, TIMSS 2015, and PIRLS 2011 for grade-4 students, combining achievement outcomes with background questionnaire information from students’ parents/caregivers. The manuscript does not describe the application of TIMSS/PIRLS complex survey weights (e.g., student sampling weights) or any replicate-weight procedure (e.g., BRR/jackknife), nor does it name any weight variable. Because the study is presented as a policy brief and focuses on regression associations and cross-national comparisons rather than ML model training, the weighting strategy is not documented; therefore, it is unclear whether weighted estimation was used. The analytic sample appears to be restricted to participating education systems with sufficient questionnaire/achievement coverage (noted in table notes about missingness thresholds), but no further preprocessing rules are specified.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This brief does not report an ML-based prediction task using PV-based cognitive achievement scores; instead, it presents regression associations and cross-national descriptive comparisons using TIMSS/PIRLS achievement outcomes at grade 4. The manuscript also does not document how missing data were handled (e.g., complete-case vs imputation) for either questionnaire-derived indices (early literacy/numeracy activity scales) or achievement outcomes. Given that PV handling and missing-data procedures are not described, this represents a reporting gap for methodological transparency.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analyses use TIMSS 2011, TIMSS 2015, and PIRLS 2011 grade-4 data from education systems that participated in all three studies (more than 30 systems). For the regression tables, the brief includes country entries where data availability meets TIMSS/PIRLS questionnaire/achievement coverage thresholds (table notes indicate that data are available for at least 50% but less than 70% of students in at least one survey, and for at least 70% but less than 85% in at least one survey). Beyond these coverage thresholds, the manuscript does not specify additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., complete-case rules, specific missingness handling, or any grade/school-type restrictions).

data.outcome_summary: This IEA Compass Brief synthesizes cross-national evidence from TIMSS 2011, TIMSS 2015, and PIRLS 2011 grade-4 data. It reports that parents/caregivers with higher educational levels engage more frequently in early literacy and numeracy activities during children’s pre-primary years (Table 1), though the strength of the association varies by country. Regression results (Tables 2 and 3) show that higher reported frequency of early literacy and early numeracy activities is positively associated with later achievement in mathematics, science, and reading after controlling for parental education; effects are described as small but statistically significant in most systems (one-tailed t-test, α=0.05). The brief also finds that attendance in institutional pre-primary education is positively related to later achievement and that parental education predicts both attendance rates and duration in many countries. Limitations include the cross-sectional nature of the data for the “nurturing environment” mechanisms, retrospective parent reporting, and lack of documented PV/missing-data handling and weighting procedures in the brief.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
